solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What actor performs in isolation?

definitions.meaning: an actor takes on a role in a play, read as two words, an article plus a role
separated or alone, away from others

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone acting alone on stage, perhaps a one-man show.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A PART, the answer is what an actor plays; as one word it means separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's own, set aside from others, is to be separately placed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: For the present perhaps nothing as starter

parts.note: someone in favour of the present might be thought against the past, ANTI plus PAST
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Suggests a present given simply as a starter, or no gift at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but belongs to the phrase: someone for the present is anti the past, ANTI + PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian first course of cold meats and vegetables, so a starter.

clue.text: Protector's army at first liable to shrink

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word army is taken
shrinking the word for liable drops its final letter

parts.note: liable to do something means prone to it

explanation.surface: A defender's army is, at the outset, inclined to back off.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron protects clothes from spills while cooking, so it is a protective garment.

clue.text: Reference books are thus improperly used by one

indicators.note: the letters of the words are thus are used wrongly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone misuses dictionaries and other reference works.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of synonyms are classic reference works; this is the Latin plural of the word for one.

clue.text: Doctor joined in group round hospital with many others

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

indicators.note: the banded word goes around the letter for hospital

parts.note: people who joined together into a group banded together
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A doctor joins a crowd gathered round a hospital with plenty of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Mob-handed is British slang for arriving in large numbers, in a gang or crowd.

clue.text: Debatable witticism about love

indicators.note: the witty remark is placed around the letter for love

parts.note: a mot (bon mot) is a witty remark
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Whether a joke about love is any good is open to argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one open to argument, still undecided, so it is arguable.

clue.text: Essential question: "What is Pyramus? A lover, or a tyrant?"

definitions.meaning: the crucial, fundamental point of a matter

definitions.text: question: "What is Pyramus? A lover, or a tyrant?"
definitions.meaning: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the weaver Bottom asks this when cast as Pyramus, so it is a line of Bottom's

explanation.surface: Presents a quotation as the key question about the hero of Shakespeare's play-within-a-play.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream who plays Pyramus, so his speech is literally a Bottom line.
explanation.definitionFit: The final total on an account came to mean the crucial, decisive factor in any matter.

clue.text: A nuisance, accepting time needed to get very fit

indicators.note: the annoying word takes in the time letter

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person

explanation.surface: An irritating person needs time to get into top shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of apt, meaning most suitable, so the fittest in the sense of best suited.

clue.text: Round sultanate, unwillingly takes guides

indicators.note: the word for unwillingly takes goes around the sultanate

parts.note: to drag is to take along reluctantly
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Someone drags along guides around an Arabian sultanate against their will.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an interpreter and guide in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking lands.

clue.text: From container, remove base

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to take a plant out of its pot
a military or transport base, a storage station

explanation.surface: An instruction to take the base off a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a whimsical coinage: DE- plus POT, like de-ice, meaning take out of a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A military supply station or bus garage is a headquarters or base of operations.

clue.text: Got up, dressed, and made to leave

explanation.surface: Someone rose, put clothes on, and was thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well turned out means smartly clothed; turning someone out means expelling them.

clue.text: Long walk needing transport and parking

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A long hike that requires a ride and somewhere to leave the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, tiring hike on foot, especially over rough country.

clue.text: Page suppressed by very severe correspondent

indicators.note: the page letter is held down inside the word for very severe

parts.note: penal means punitive, extremely harsh

explanation.surface: A page of writing has been censored by a harsh letter-writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is someone you exchange letters with, a regular letter-writer.

clue.text: Contracted military base to cover most of coast

indicators.note: the fort word goes over and around the trimmed coast word

parts.note: a fort is a fortified military post

indicators.note: the final letter of the coast word is lost

parts.note: the shore is the coastline

explanation.surface: A military base is contracted to defend most of the coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: A name used in shortened form, abbreviated, as in Tom being Thomas for brevity.

clue.text: In a flash, from a distance one shows where the game is

indicators.note: the following letters are put in the word for a flash

parts.note: a spark is a brief flash of light
afar means from far away
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone spots from far away, in a flash, where the quarry is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests a sport or contest but means wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild animals roam enclosures that visitors drive through at this kind of zoo.

clue.text: Move acrobatically, hearing of a certain attack

indicators.note: the phrase is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a certain attack is some assault

explanation.surface: An acrobat's manoeuvre described as hearing about a specific attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipping heels over head through a full rotation is a classic gymnastic manoeuvre.

clue.text: Girl is waiting for blues

parts.note: Miss is a title for a girl
a matter that pends is awaiting decision

explanation.surface: A girl is waiting because she feels sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blues' reads as a noun for sadness but is a verb: to blue money is British slang for squandering it.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue cash is to squander it, the same as wasting it foolishly.

clue.text: Start of March cold and damp from the east? On the contrary

indicators.note: an across entry read from the east runs right to left, backwards

parts.note: raw weather is cold and damp

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word March

explanation.surface: Describes chilly, wet weather as March begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' does double duty: the clue gives M then the reversed RAW, so the order is swapped, and the result is the opposite of cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of the clue's cold, so heated is the contrary of chilly weather.

clue.text: Dead at last in mortuary, horribly bloody woman

indicators.note: the letters are horribly mangled, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of a woman dead at last in a mortuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last in' says where D sits in the fodder before the shuffle signalled by 'horribly'; the result is an anagram of MORTUARY plus D.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Mary I of England was nicknamed Bloody Mary for burning Protestants.

clue.text: Steps round an elevated aperture

indicators.note: the stairs word goes around the word an

parts.note: a flight is a series of stairs

explanation.surface: A staircase winding round to a high opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular window set above a door, so an opening high up.

clue.text: Woman's address in fine city

indicators.note: the title is put inside the word for fine

parts.note: OK means fine
Ms is a title for addressing a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's home address is in a pleasant city.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large Siberian city in Russia, on the Irtysh river.

clue.text: Legendary German woman, briefly, that employer's taken in

indicators.note: the woman's name is held inside the shortened word
the word that is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before shortening
Ann is a woman's name
a user is someone who employs something

explanation.surface: A German woman of legend, in short, recruited by an employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last letter of 'that', and the 's is 'has', so the shortened word has the woman taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight and minnesinger of German legend, hero of Wagner's opera of the same name.

clue.text: Ply with beer, knocked back with tablet?

indicators.note: the beer word is turned backwards, a pun on drinking

parts.note: lager is a type of beer
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Plying someone with beer, downed alongside a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain lavishly, plying a guest with food and drink, is the same idea.

clue.text: Sort of order that's typically American

definitions.meaning: perfect neatness is called this kind of order
the idiom as American as this dessert

explanation.surface: Something neat and quintessentially American.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape tidiness is called by this dessert's name, and the dish is a byword for Americanness.

clue.text: Particular language to investigate Monet's work, as it were?

indicators.note: flags the literal reading of going into: the verb is placed inside the art word

parts.note: Monet's work is art, being paintings
to investigate is to go into something, so the word go is entered into what follows

explanation.surface: Studying a painter's work requires its own jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: To investigate is to 'go into'; read literally, GO goes into ART, giving AR(GO)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is jargon or slang peculiar to one group, a specialised vocabulary.

clue.text: College port finally — following this perhaps?

parts.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University

indicators.note: the last letter of the word port is taken

explanation.surface: A college dinner where port comes last, after another wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue says port follows this wine: at a formal dinner port traditionally comes after the red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A red Bordeaux wine served before the port at a traditional dinner.

clue.text: Spicy sandwiches — spit half out

indicators.note: half of the spit word is put out, leaving the first five letters

parts.note: a rotisserie is a rotating spit for roasting

explanation.surface: Food so spicy that you spit half of it out.
explanation.definitionFit: South Asian flatbreads, often wrapped round a curry filling, served as spiced wraps.

clue.text: Tart female? That's academic

parts.note: a pro, short for prostitute, is a tart

explanation.surface: A sharp woman who is scholarly.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal shortening for a university professor, a senior lecturer.

clue.text: Informally, about to get large lizard away from an area

indicators.note: the area letter is removed from the lizard

parts.note: a goanna is a large Australian monitor lizard

explanation.surface: Someone is about to get a big lizard out of a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual speech shortening of going to, used for intending to do something soon.

clue.text: Unfairly claimed school has no boundaries — kept in

indicators.note: the school name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school
gated means confined to school as a punishment

explanation.surface: A school that lacks walls claims pupils were kept in after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to take or claim something without justification, so seized.

clue.text: Worth mentioning: crossing south summit take base from the rear

indicators.note: the reversed base word goes across and around the other pieces
the base word is read starting from its back end

parts.note: the foot is the base of something
a peak is a mountain summit

explanation.surface: Climbers crossing south to the summit set out from base camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually in negatives, as in nothing to speak of, meaning nothing notable enough to mention.

clue.text: Not a serious piece, a shocker

indicators.note: a piece of the words Not a serious is taken from within them

explanation.surface: Says a frivolous piece of writing is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A stun gun firing electrified darts, which delivers an incapacitating jolt.
